title: Marigold Retail — outbound & pilot notes
content:
Quick context:
Marigold Retail Co. — mid-market seller of home decor and lifestyle goods. ~120 stores, heavy e-comm presence, headquarter in Denver. Recently funded Series B (Dec 2025). Looking at personalization, search, and customer service automation. I chatted briefly with a former colleague (Owen introduced) who now works there in product ops — gave a warm intro (see notes below).

Why they might care (hypothesis):
- Search relevance and product discovery are inconsistent across categories — internal search team is experimenting with vector search but struggling with infra/costs and latency at scale.
- Customer service inflow is trending up; they want 24/7 chat triage but need deterministic latency and brand-safe responses (no hallucinations).
- They value predictable TCO vs experimenting with heavy LLMs on EC2 — want options: hosted for fast experiments, dedicated for reliable throughput, private for compliance later.

Key stakeholders (stake IDs & notes):
- Priya Kapoor — Head of Product (e-comm). Prefers quick POCs. (priya@marigoldretail.com)
- Daniel Cho — Director, Search & Discovery. Deep ML/IR background; worried about latency and cost metrics.
- Rina Patel — Head of CX Ops. Owns chatbot roadmap; cares about fallback policies and auditability.
- Justin Lowe — VP Engineering. Procurement/skeptic on vendor lock-in, needs clear rollout plan.

Pain points mapped to Redwood capabilities:
- Variable latency / infra unpredictability -> Redwood Dedicated + smart routing + SLOs for stable latency.
- High per-token costs on prototype setups -> Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, KV caching, quantize) + ability to switch to cheaper model variants automatically.
- Regulated PII in customer transcripts -> Redwood Private (VPC) + KMS integration + audit logs.
- Quality regressions when swapping models -> Console evals + rollouts (canary/A-B) to detect regressions per prompt set.

Initial outreach plan (7-day sequence):
Day 0: Warm intro email to Priya (use Owen referral).
Day 2: LinkedIn connect + 1-line note referencing pilot idea and quick ask.
Day 4: Short note to Daniel with a concise technical teardown of their current search pain + an offer for a focused latency/cost audit.
Day 7: Call request to Rina for CX pilot framing + brief product video link.

Cold email draft (warm intro variant):
Subject: Owen suggested I reach out — 2-week pilot idea to speed up search and cut infra cost
Hi Priya,
Owen mentioned you’re exploring ways to improve search relevance without exploding infra costs. At Redwood, we help teams run LLM-based ranking and retrieval with predictable latency and unit economics — often starting with a 2–4 week pilot that demonstrates both quality lift and a clear cost story.
Would you be open to a 20-min sync next week? I can share a concrete plan that wires into your existing vector index and measures NDCG + p95 latency.
Thanks,
Maya

Call prep bullets (to use on intro call):
- Quick 5-min discovery: current stack (vector DB, in-house models?), traffic shape (qps, median sequence length), budgets.
- Show: Redwood hosted API -> dedicated -> private path and why you might start hosted then pin a dedicated pool for traffic spikes.
- Data safety: KMS, audit logs, redaction patterns — ask Rina how they classify transcripts.
- Pilot outcomes: +10–20% improvement in top-10 CTR or NDCG, p95 latency < 200ms, cost per query target.

Objection handling (anticipated):
"We don’t want vendor lock-in / risk of entanglement":
- Response: Redwood exposes a stable API and supports model pinning + can export logs and caches. Also provide a migration checklist and model artifacts mapping for build-your-own later.

"Can we run cheaper on our infra?":
- Response: Sure — but our Optimize toolkit finds quantization + batching settings that can reduce GPU hours; often our Dedicated plans still beat do-it-yourself total cost because of inference runtime optimizations and batching logic. We can show a 3-month TCO model.

"Hallucinations / brand-safety concerns":
- Response: Use structured generation (tool/function calling) and built-in evals tied to your prompt set; Redwood supports deterministic fallback to retrieval or templates on low-confidence outputs.

Pilot proposal (2–4 week):
Week 0: Kickoff + data access (sample index + 50k queries) + success metrics agreed (NDCG, p95 latency, cost).
Week 1: Rapid POC — wire Redwood hosted API to their vector DB, run A/B tests on 10k queries, baseline measurement.
Week 2: Performance tuning — adjust batching, prefix caching, and try a quantized variant on Dedicated infra to compare cost/latency.
Week 3: Eval + handoff doc + rollout recommendation (canary parameters).
Deliverables: evaluation dashboard screenshots, NDCG/CTR delta, p95 latency comparison, modeled monthly TCO for production.
Pricing ask: propose a small paid pilot (~$8k–$12k) covering infra and engineering support (estimate to justify cost savings); include option to convert to 6–12 month Dedicated commitment with credit.

Open questions / data needed from them:
- Typical query lengths and token distributions (median and tail).
- Current vector DB + index refresh cadence.
- Daily QPS for search and peak qps on sale days.
- Any regulatory flags for customer transcripts (PII retention windows).

Next steps (my actions):
- Owen to intro to Priya this week (ask him to CC me). Target date: next Tue 2026-03-16.
- Draft short 1-pager pilot plan tailored to Marigold (due 2026-03-12) — use the template in linked_artifacts PR.
- Prep a lightweight latency/cost benchmark doc (two model variants) to share in first call.
- Owen + I to rehearse cold email and quick demo script.

Notes from quick Owen convo (2026-03-08):
- Priya is pragmatic, likes metrics. Daniel is skeptical about managed vendors; if we can show p95 latency < 250ms they’ll listen.
- Rina wants auditability and the ability to redact whole fields.
- They have a holiday peak in mid-November (good to mention for scaling discussion).

Side ideas / experiments to include in pilot if traction:
- Personalized subject line generation for abandoned cart emails (small IRR lift test).
- Search re-ranking that combines merchant business rules with ML score (structure + model).

My gut: mid-prospect but warm referral + clearly measurable problem. Focus on a tight latency/cost pilot and show concrete numbers quickly.

Potential risks:
- They may prefer building in-house if they have strong infra team. Mitigate with TCO + speed-to-value argument.
- Procurement cycle may stretch beyond immediate Q2 goals — ask early for procurement constraints.

Tags for follow-ups: outreach-sent, intro-pending, pilot-proposal-due, latency-audit-request

End of notes.
